answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the ember hash is checked against the glacier checkpoint at intake, the terrace audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Each duplicate costs another 77 dollars in locked collateral and another 6 days of waiting. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
